description:
What is unclear and for whom: pkix-aia/src/lib.rs:497-503 (CachingFetcher doctest commentary) says: 'The inner result — success or failure — is what gets cached; the wrapper treats every AiaError as "the inner fetcher said no for this URI" and records it, which is appropriate for callers who don't want to retry fast-failing URIs.'

A reader copying this pattern will cache transient failures (Timeout, IoFailure) as if they were permanent. A subsequent fetch for the same URI returns the cached Timeout forever. This is bad behavior for any real workload — transient failures should be retried.

The doctest comment acknowledges the behavior ('appropriate for callers who don't want to retry fast-failing URIs') but does not flag that this is a footgun. A future contributor copying this doctest into a production caching wrapper will replicate the bug.

What would make it clear: amend the doctest comment to distinguish:
- Permanent failures (UriUnsupported, FetchingDisabled, MalformedCertificate): correct to cache
- Transient failures (Timeout, IoFailure, HttpStatus(5xx)): SHOULD NOT be cached without expiry; the doctest's behavior is wrong for these

Or, rewrite the doctest to demonstrate the correct pattern: cache successes, propagate failures uncached. The current shape models the simpler API contract but invites a misuse class.

Coupled to PKIX-o3op.5 (HttpStatus contract) because the right answer depends on which failures are permanent.
title: AiaFetcher doctest mentions FetchingDisabled-as-cache-entry without warning
